title: Bug: wait_for_url() exits immediately under set -e due to ((c++)) when c=0
description:
In core.sh line ~476 and standalone.sh line ~472, the wait_for_url function contains:
```bash
function wait_for_url() { local u="${1}" t="${2:-30}" c=0; until quiet curl -s --head --request GET "$u"; do sleep 1; ((c++)); ... done; return 0; }
```

When c=0, the arithmetic expression ((c++)) evaluates to 0 (post-increment returns old value), which is falsy. Under `set -e`, this causes the script to exit immediately on the first retry iteration, making the function always fail after one sleep.

Fix: Replace ((c++)) with ((c++)) || true, or better: c=$((c + 1))

title: Bug: E_USAGE and E_SUCCESS undefined in main.sh
description:
main.sh line 79 and 82 use $E_USAGE and $E_SUCCESS which are standard sysexit.h constants but are never defined in the codebase.

Line 79: exit "$E_USAGE"
Line 82: return "$E_SUCCESS"

These evaluate to empty strings, causing exit "" (exit code 0) and return "" (return 0), which silently masks the intended exit code semantics.

Fix: Define E_USAGE=64 and E_SUCCESS=0 at the top of main.sh, or use literal values directly.

title: Inconsistency: timestamp() differs between core.sh and standalone.sh
description:
core.sh implements timestamp() with a Bash version check for 4.2+ to use printf %()T format with a fallback to date:
```bash
function timestamp() {
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -gt 4 || ( "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -eq 4 && "${BASH_VERSINFO[1]}" -ge 2 ) ]]; then
        printf '%(%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)T\n' -1
    else
        date +'%Y%m%d_%H%M%S'
    fi
}
```

standalone.sh (the build output) strips this to a simple:
```bash
function timestamp() { date +'%Y%m%d_%H%M%S'; }
```

The build process (build.sh) strips the version-aware implementation, producing different runtime behavior. This is caused by build.sh sed pattern that removes lines between BOILERPLATE_CORE_START marker, which includes the version check.

Fix: Update build.sh to preserve the full timestamp() implementation, or unify both implementations.

title: Inconsistency: slugify() produces different output in core.sh vs standalone.sh
description:
core.sh slugify() uses Bash 4+ parameter expansion for lowercasing and converts spaces to underscores BEFORE the tr step:
```bash
function slugify() {
    local str="${1,,}" # Lowercase
    str="${str// /_}" # Spaces to underscores
    echo "$str" | tr -sc '[:alnum:]' '-' | tr -s '-' | sed 's/^-//;s/-$//'
}
```

standalone.sh slugify() pipes through tr for lowercasing and does NOT convert spaces to underscores:
```bash
function slugify() { echo "${1}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -sc '[:alnum:]' '-' | tr -s '-' | sed 's/^-//;s/-$//'; }
```

Behavioral difference: "Hello World" produces "hello_world" in core.sh but "hello-world" in standalone.sh.

Fix: Make both implementations identical. The core.sh behavior (spaces to underscores before tr) is likely the intended behavior.

title: Test gap: 68 functions in core.sh but only 6 tests exist
description:
core.sh defines 68 functions but only 6 tests exist across all test files (3 in core.bats, 3 in build.bats).

Untested critical functions include:
- retry() - uses eval, has the ((attempt++)) pattern
- wait_for_url() - has the ((c++)) bug
- lock() / unlock() - concurrency primitives
- load_env() - security-sensitive (exports arbitrary env vars)
- cron_init() - changes file descriptors
- safe_mode() - changes shell options
- error_trap() / cleanup() - error handling
- is_empty() - data validation
- is_container() - platform detection
- version_gt() - version comparison
- get_json_val() - JSON parsing
- is_online() - network check
- run_as_root() / sudo_escalate() - privilege escalation
- check_superuser() - access control

Only is_sourced(), slugify(), and is_int() are tested.

Fix: Add tests for critical public functions, especially error handling, retry logic, file operations, and validation functions.

title: Security: echo -e used throughout for messages that may contain backslash sequences
description:
The log(), out(), overwrite(), and append() functions all use echo -e to output messages. If message content contains backslash sequences (\n, \t, \a, \x, etc.), they will be interpreted rather than displayed literally.

Affected functions in core.sh:
- Line 210: echo -e "$log_msg" >&2 (log)
- Line 211: echo -e "$log_msg" | sed ... (log file output)
- Line 233: echo -e "$*" >&1 (out stdout)
- Line 234: echo -e "$*" >&2 (out stderr)
- Line 246: echo -e "$*" > "$target" (overwrite)
- Line 256: echo -e "$*" >> "$target" (append)

This is a security concern because:
1. Log messages containing attacker-controlled input could produce unexpected output
2. File content written via overwrite()/append() could be corrupted
3. echo -e behavior differs between bash implementations

Fix: Replace echo -e with printf '%b\n' or use echo without -e flag.

title: Security: retry() uses eval without input sanitization
description:
The retry() function uses eval to execute the command string:
```bash
function retry() {
    local -r -i max_attempts="$1"; shift; local -r cmd="$@"; local -i attempt=1
    until eval "$cmd"; do
        ...
    done
}
```

eval executes arbitrary shell commands from the cmd string. If cmd comes from user input or an untrusted source, this is a code injection vulnerability.

Fix: Replace eval with a safer execution method, or document that the command must be trusted.

title: Inconsistency: error_trap() parameter quoting differs between core.sh and standalone.sh
description:
In core.sh, error_trap() uses quoted parameters:
```bash
local -r line_no="$1"
local -r fn_name="$2"
```

In standalone.sh, the same function uses unquoted parameters:
```bash
local -r line_no=$1
local -r fn_name=$2
```

While this specific case is unlikely to cause issues (LINENO and FUNCNAME don't contain spaces), it's an inconsistency that suggests the build process may be producing non-deterministic output.

Fix: Ensure build.sh produces byte-identical output from core.sh.

title: Bug: is_container() may fail under set -e when /proc/1/cgroup is unreadable
description:
The is_container() function:
```bash
function is_container() { [[ -f /.dockerenv ]] || grep -qE "docker|lxc|containerd" /proc/1/cgroup 2>/dev/null || return 1; }
```

While the `|| return 1` handles the grep failure, if /proc/1/cgroup doesn't exist or is unreadable, grep returns 2 (error) not 1 (no match). Under set -e, the grep exit code 2 would propagate before reaching the || clause in some bash versions.

The 2>/dev/null suppresses stderr but doesn't change the exit code behavior.

Fix: Add explicit error handling: `grep -qE "..." /proc/1/cgroup 2>/dev/null || true`
closeReason: False positive: commands in || chains are exempt from set -e. grep exit code 2 (file not found) is caught by || return 1.

title: Bug: is_online() pings google.com by hostname - DNS resolution failure masquerades as offline
description:
The is_online() function:
```bash
function is_online() { for h in "8.8.8.8" "1.1.1.1" "google.com"; do ping -c 1 -W 1 "$h" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; done; return 1; }
```

The third check uses hostname "google.com" instead of an IP. If the system has network connectivity but DNS is down, this check will always fail. Combined with the fact that pinging a non-existent host returns 1 (not 0), a system with working network but broken DNS would be reported as offline.

Fix: Use only IP addresses for connectivity checks, or add a DNS-specific check.

title: Bug: load_env() regex skips comment lines with leading whitespace
description:
The load_env() function checks for comments with:
```bash
[[ "$k" =~ ^#.*$ || -z "$k" ]] && continue
```

The regex ^#.*$ only matches lines starting with # at position 0. Lines like "  # comment" (with leading whitespace) would NOT be skipped, causing the variable name to be "  #" which would then be exported as an invalid variable.

Fix: Use a more permissive regex: [[ "$k" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] to catch indented comments.

title: Bug: build.sh lacks set -euo pipefail and has incomplete temp file cleanup
description:
build.sh is missing strict mode (set -euo pipefail). If any command fails:
1. The script continues executing, potentially producing a corrupted standalone.sh
2. The rm on line 39 could delete temp files from a previous failed run

Additionally, tmp_standalone (created on line 28) is never cleaned up if the script fails after line 28 but before line 39.

Fix: Add set -euo pipefail at the top of build.sh, and add a trap for temp file cleanup.

title: Bug: retry() accepts empty command and succeeds
description:
The retry() function:
```bash
function retry() {
    local -r -i max_attempts="$1"; shift; local -r cmd="$@"; local -i attempt=1
    until eval "$cmd"; do
        ...
    done
}
```

If called with only max_attempts and no command (e.g., retry 3), shift removes the first arg, and cmd becomes empty string. eval "" succeeds (exit code 0), so retry returns 0 immediately without executing anything.

Fix: Add a check after shift: [[ -z "${1:-}" ]] && die "retry() requires a command".

title: Bug: load_env() exports variables from lines without = separator
description:
The load_env() function reads lines with:
```bash
while IFS='=' read -r k v || [[ -n "$k" ]]; do
    [[ "$k" =~ ^#.*$ || -z "$k" ]] && continue
    ...
    export "${k}=${v}"
done < "$f"
```

Lines without an = sign (e.g., "INVALID_LINE") would set k="INVALID_LINE" and v="", then export "INVALID_LINE=" as an empty variable. This silently creates invalid environment variables.

Fix: Add a check: [[ "$k" != *=* ]] && continue (skip lines without =).

title: Bug: lock() has a TOCTOU race condition between check and write
description:
The lock() function:
```bash
function lock() {
    local scope="${1:-system}"
    local l
    if [[ "${scope}" == "user" ]]; then
        l="/tmp/${__base}.${UID}.lock"
    else
        l="/tmp/${__base}.lock"
    fi
    if [[ -e "$l" ]]; then
        local p=$(cat "$l")
        kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null && die "Already running (PID: ${p})"
    fi
    echo "$$" > "$l"
    readonly __lockfile="$l"
}
```

Between checking if the lock file exists and writing to it, another process could create the lock file. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition.

Fix: Use mkdir (which is atomic) or use flock for file locking.
